option_a: Have one valence electron which they easily lose

question_text: Which of the following is an alkali metal?
explanation: Sodium is in Group I.

question_text: Which of the following is an alkaline earth metal?
explanation: Calcium is in Group II.

question_text: Which of the following is a halogen?
explanation: Chlorine is in Group VII.

question_text: Which of the following is a noble gas?
explanation: Argon is in Group 0.

question_text: Across a period from left to right, atomic radius
explanation: Increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer.

question_text: Down a group, atomic radius
explanation: Additional electron shells increase the size of the atom.

question_text: Across a period from left to right, ionisation energy generally
explanation: Stronger nuclear attraction makes it harder to remove electrons.

question_text: Down a group, ionisation energy generally
explanation: Electrons are further from the nucleus and easier to remove.

question_text: Across a period from left to right, electronegativity generally
explanation: Non-metallic character increases across a period.

question_text: Down a group, electronegativity generally
explanation: Atoms get larger; the nucleus holds outer electrons less tightly.

question_text: Across a period from left to right, metallic character
explanation: Elements become more non-metallic across a period.

question_text: Down a group, metallic character
explanation: Elements become more metallic down a group.

question_text: Across a period from left to right, electron affinity generally
explanation: Non-metals have a greater tendency to gain electrons.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the largest atomic radius?
explanation: Atomic radius increases down a group; K is in period 4.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the smallest atomic radius?
explanation: Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group; Li is at the top left.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the highest electronegativity?
explanation: Fluorine is the most electronegative element.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the lowest electronegativity?
explanation: Caesium has very low electronegativity (bottom left of the table).

question_text: Which of the following elements has the highest ionisation energy?
explanation: Ionisation energy increases across a period; Cl is furthest right.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the lowest ionisation energy?
explanation: Ionisation energy decreases down a group; Rb is lowest.

question_text: Which of the following is a transition metal?
explanation: Transition metals are in the d-block (Groups 3-12); Iron is a transition metal.

question_text: Which of the following is a property of transition metals?
explanation: Transition metals commonly form coloured compounds.

question_text: Which of the following is a property of transition metals?
option_b: They have only one oxidation state
explanation: Transition metals have variable oxidation states.

question_text: Which of the following is a property of transition metals?
explanation: Transition metals and their compounds are good catalysts.

question_text: Which of the following elements is in Period 3?
explanation: Sodium (Z=11) has configuration 2,8,1 (three shells).

question_text: Which of the following elements is in Group 2?
explanation: Magnesium (Z=12) has configuration 2,8,2 (2 valence electrons).

question_text: Which of the following elements is in Group 17?
explanation: Chlorine (Z=17) has configuration 2,8,7 (7 valence electrons).

question_text: Which of the following elements is in Period 2?
explanation: Lithium (Z=3) has configuration 2,1 (two shells).

question_text: Which block of the periodic table contains the most non-metals?
explanation: The p-block contains most non-metals.

question_text: Which of the following elements is a metalloid?
explanation: Silicon is a metalloid (properties between metals and non-metals).

question_text: Which of the following statements about the periodic table is correct?
option_a: Elements in the same period have the same number of valence electrons
option_b: Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties
option_c: Elements in the same group have the same number of electron shells
option_d: Elements in the same period have the same atomic mass
explanation: Elements in the same group have similar chemical properties due to identical valence electron configurations.

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a property of metals?
explanation: Metals are malleable, not brittle.

question_text: Which of the following is NOT a property of non-metals?
explanation: Non-metals are generally brittle, not malleable.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the highest metallic character?
explanation: Metallic character decreases across a period; Na is furthest left.

question_text: Which of the following elements has the highest non-metallic character?
explanation: Non-metallic character increases across a period; Si is furthest right among these.
